mainTopic: The snake and the lion as damagers, the difference between תם and מועד, and related אגדה
overview: The amud opens by fixing the wording of a ברייתא so that רבי אלעזר says 'the snake', not 'also the snake'. That way he treats the snake as always מועד, just as he does in the משנה. Next, שמואל rules that if a lion in רשות הרבים clawed its prey and ate it, the owner is פטור, because that is normal eating (שן). If it tore the prey apart and then ate, the owner is חייב. The גמרא defends this from a פסוק about lions tearing prey: they tear only to feed their family. It then faces a ברייתא where a lion tore and ate and the owner pays full damage. רב נחמן בר יצחק reads that ברייתא as two separate cases. רבינא reads it as a tame lion according to רבי אלעזר, but that reading ends with an unanswered קשיא. A new משנה teaches that a תם pays half damage from its own body, while a מועד pays full damage from the owner's best property (עלייה). The גמרא proves this meaning from the burial of חזקיהו, which leads into a series of אגדה passages about royal burials and ירמיהו's enemies.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר adds the snake
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אלעזר saying that the snake is 'also' included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: Also the snake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of a ברייתא, where רבי אלעזר adds the snake to the list of dangerous animals. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'also' suggests the snake is just like the other animals on the list. רבי אלעזר holds that those animals are not מועד once they are tame. So 'also' seems to mean the snake follows that same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too. It puts something in the same group as what came before.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
Also the snake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from just before this section, which listed wild animals that are מועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the ברייתא, רבי אלעזר includes the snake with the other wild animals, using the word 'also.'

steps.title: The משנה shows the snake is different from the others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: in our משנה, רבי אלעזר treats the snake as different from the other animals, so how can the ברייתא say 'also'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: רבי אלעזר says, when these animals are tame they are not מועד, but the snake is always מועד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא with a משנה that quotes רבי אלעזר. In the משנה, he says the snake stays מועד even when it is tame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אלעזר splits the animals into two groups. The tame wild animals are not מועד, but the snake is always מועד. So 'also the snake' cannot mean the snake is like the others, because that would make it lose its מועד status when tame.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn? This opens a challenge from a משנה.
An animal known to cause damage, so its owner pays full damages

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'also the snake' as making the snake more dangerous than the others. The problem is the opposite: 'also' makes the snake sound just like the others, which would mean it is NOT מועד when tame. The משנה says it always is.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn (in the Mishnah):
Rabbi Elazar says:
When they are domesticated,
they are not considered forewarned;
but the snake is always forewarned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording 'also' in the ברייתא from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'אף' in רבי אלעזר's statement in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Also' puts the snake in the same group as the other animals. But in the משנה, רבי אלעזר separates the snake, which is always מועד, from the others, which lose that status when tame.

steps.title: Read it as 'the snake,' not 'also the snake'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by changing the wording of the ברייתא to just 'the snake.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: the snake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem by fixing the wording of the ברייתא. It drops the word 'also.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'also,' רבי אלעזר is singling the snake out instead of grouping it with the other animals. Now the ברייתא matches the משנה: only the snake stays מועד even when tame.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach it this way. It is used to fix how a ברייתא should be worded.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, the snake stands alone. It stays מועד even when tame, while the other wild animals do not.

phrases.english: Teach (it as): A snake.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is adjusting the wording, so read רבי אלעזר as saying 'the snake' without the word 'also.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fixing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says 'also the snake,' grouping it with the tame animals that are not מועד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא should say 'the snake,' setting it apart as always מועד, just like the משנה.

steps.title: שמואל's ruling on a lion that kills in public
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules on a lion in רשות הרבים. If it pounced and ate, the owner is פטור. If it tore the prey apart and ate, the owner is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: A lion in רשות הרבים: if it pounced and ate, the owner is exempt. If it tore apart and ate, the owner is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ruling by שמואל about a lion that kills an animal in a public place. The owner's liability depends on how the lion killed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases happen in רשות הרבים, and in both the lion eats the prey. The only difference is the way of killing, pouncing versus tearing apart. That one detail decides whether the owner pays.

keyTerms.meaning: Public domain, a place where many people walk
Pounced on or clawed its prey

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
A lion in the public domain:
If it clawed (its prey) and ate it, (the owner is) exempt.
If it tore (its prey) apart and ate it, (the owner is) liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, still about wild animals like the lion from the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lion in רשות הרבים: pounced and ate means the owner is פטור; tore apart and ate means the owner is חייב.

steps.title: Why pouncing is exempt and tearing is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains שמואל. Pouncing is the lion's normal way of eating, so it counts as שן, which is exempt in רשות הרבים. Tearing apart is not its normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Pounced and ate, exempt: since its normal way is to pounce, it is like an animal eating fruits and vegetables. That is שן in רשות הרבים, so the owner is exempt. Tearing apart is not its normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind שמואל's two rulings. It compares the lion's normal pouncing to a cow eating produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a lion, pouncing and eating is simply how it eats, just as eating fruit is normal for a cow. So it falls under שן, and שן is exempt in רשות הרבים. Tearing apart is not the lion's normal way, so it loses the שן exemption, and the owner pays even in a public place.

keyTerms.meaning: Its normal way, its usual behavior
Tooth: damage from an animal eating for its own benefit. It is exempt in רשות הרבים.
Fruits and vegetables, the classic example of שן

steps.whatToRemember: An animal's normal way of eating counts as שן, even when it eats another animal. So a lion that pounces and eats in רשות הרבים leaves its owner פטור. Acting outside its normal way removes that exemption.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that שן is defined by what is normal for that species, not by what is being eaten. That is a key idea for sorting the categories of damage.

phrases.english: (If) it clawed and ate, (the owner is) exempt,
since its normal manner is to claw (its prey),

phrases.aramaic: הָוֵה לֵיהּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָכְלָה פֵּירוֹת וִירָקוֹת,
phrases.english: it is like (an animal) that ate fruits and vegetables,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוֵי לֵיהּ שֵׁן בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, וּפָטוּר.
phrases.english: which is Tooth in the public domain, and is exempt.
(But if) it tore apart, that is not its normal manner.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves the ending unsaid: since this isn't normal, it isn't שן, so the owner is חייב.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַס וְאָכַל פָּטוּר – כֵּיוָן דְּאוֹרְחֵיהּ לְמִידְרַס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind שמואל's ruling in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pouncing and eating is the lion's normal eating, so it counts as שן, which is exempt in רשות הרבים. Tearing apart is not normal, so the owner is liable.

steps.title: A verse shows lions do tear their prey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's claim that tearing is not a lion's normal way, citing a פסוק that describes a lion tearing prey.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that tearing apart is not the lion's normal way? But the פסוק says: 'The lion tears apart enough for its cubs'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation of שמואל from step 5. If tearing is not normal for a lion, why does a פסוק describe lions tearing their prey?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said pouncing is the lion's normal way and tearing is not. A פסוק in נחום describes a lion tearing prey as a natural thing it does. If tearing is normal, then tearing and eating should count as שן, and the owner should be פטור in רשות הרבים, the opposite of what שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? (introduces a challenge to an implication)
Its normal way, its usual behavior
But isn't it written...? (challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: Is this to say that tearing apart is not its normal way?
But isn't it written: "The lion tears apart enough for its cubs"!
phrases.notes: נחום ב:יג

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דִּטְרֵיפָה לָאו אוֹרְחֵיהּ הוּא? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in step 5 for שמואל's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 5 that tearing is not a lion's normal way of eating.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק describes lions tearing prey as natural behavior, so tearing seems to be normal for them.

steps.title: The lion tears only to feed its family
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes through each part of the פסוק and shows that every time the lion tears, it is for its cubs, lionesses, or den, not for its own meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It tears for its cubs. But it says 'and strangles for its lionesses'! That is for its lionesses. But it says 'and fills its lairs with prey'! That is for its lairs. But it says 'and its dens with torn prey'! That is for its dens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק talks about a lion tearing prey to bring food to its family. Each time the questioner points to another phrase in the פסוק, the גמרא gives the same answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is the purpose of the tearing. A lion tears prey when it is gathering food for others. When it eats on the spot for itself, its normal way is to pounce and eat, so שמואל's ruling still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of, in order to provide for

steps.confusionAlert: Each quoted phrase with an exclamation mark is another small challenge, and each 'בִּשְׁבִיל' line is the answer. It is one back-and-forth repeated four times.

phrases.english: That is for its cubs.
But it says: "And it strangles for its lionesses"!
That is for its lionesses.
But it says: "And it fills its lairs with prey"!
That is for its lairs.
But it says: "And its dens with torn prey"!
That is for its dens.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Series of short קשיא and תירוץ pairs
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific purpose (feeding others)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to show that lions normally tear prey in every situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Lions tear prey when providing for their family, but when eating for themselves their normal way is pouncing.

steps.title: A ברייתא makes the owner pay full damage for tearing and eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from a ברייתא where an animal tore and ate in the victim's yard and the owner pays full damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: Likewise, a wild animal that entered the victim's yard, tore apart an animal and ate the meat, the owner pays full damage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge, this time from a ברייתא. In the ברייתא, an animal tears and eats, and its owner pays full damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying full damage in the victim's yard fits שן, which is damage done in the animal's normal way. So the ברייתא seems to treat tearing and eating as normal behavior. That goes against שמואל's claim that tearing is not normal.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא...? (challenge from a ברייתא)
The yard of the injured party

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: And likewise, a wild animal
that entered the yard of the injured party,
tore apart an animal and ate the meat:
the owner pays full damage!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: וְכֵן חַיָּה שֶׁנִּכְנְסָה לַחֲצַר הַנִּיזָּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the פסוק challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a new challenge from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that tearing and eating is not a lion's normal way.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives full damage for tearing and eating, treating it as normal eating (שן), which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: The animal tore the prey to save it for later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא is about an animal that tore its prey in order to store it for later.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where it tore the prey to leave it for later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case in the ברייתא. The animal tore the prey to store it, not to eat it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the lion in the פסוק that tears prey for later use, tearing to store food is normal for a lion. That is why the owner pays full damage in the ברייתא. שמואל was talking about tearing in order to eat right away, which is not normal.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrowed case)
To leave it, to put it aside for later

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
Where it tore the prey in order to leave it for later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא challenge from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that tearing in order to eat is normal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about tearing to store food, which is normal; שמואל is about tearing to eat right away.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says it ate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא clearly says the animal ate the meat, not that it stored it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא says 'and ate'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer in step 9. The ברייתא says the animal ate the meat, so how can it be about saving it for later?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 9 seems to clash with the wording of the ברייתא. If the animal ate the meat, it does not look like it was storing it.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches...! (pointing to the wording of a source)

phrases.english: But it teaches "and ate"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about tearing in order to store the prey.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly says the animal ate, which does not fit an animal that was storing its prey.

steps.title: It changed its mind and ate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the animal first tore the prey to store it, then changed its mind and ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where it changed its mind and ate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its answer. The tearing was done to store the prey, and only afterward did the animal decide to eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is why the animal tore the prey. Because the tearing was for storing, which is normal, the owner still pays full damage even though the animal ate in the end.

phrases.english: Where it changed its mind and ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating seemed to show the animal never meant to store the prey.
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal tore the prey to store it, then decided to eat it afterward.

steps.title: We cannot know what the animal intended
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer: there is no way to know the animal's intention, and the same doubt would apply to שמואל's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know? And besides, in שמואל's case too, maybe that is what happened?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from steps 9 and 11 with two problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, we cannot see inside an animal's mind, so we cannot tell whether it tore the prey to store it or to eat it. Second, if we accept this idea, then any lion in שמואל's case might also have torn to store, which would make tearing normal, and then the owner should be פטור in רשות הרבים. So the challenge from the ברייתא is back on the table.
steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to explain the ברייתא as tearing to store the prey fails. You cannot know an animal's intent, and the same doubt would undo שמואל's own ruling. The challenge from the ברייתא still stands for now.

phrases.english: How do we know?
phrases.notes: He means: how can we know what the animal was planning when it tore the prey?

phrases.english: And furthermore, in שמואל's case too:
maybe it is like this?
phrases.notes: Meaning: maybe שמואל's lion also tore its prey to store it, which would make the owner פטור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer built in steps 9 and 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole answer that the ברייתא is about tearing to store, followed by a change of mind.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An animal's intent cannot be known, and the same uncertainty would undermine שמואל's own case.

steps.title: The ברייתא is listing two separate cases
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge from the ברייתא by reading it as two separate cases. A lion that tore its prey to store it, or a lion that clawed its prey and ate it, pays full damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The ברייתא is teaching separate cases. If the lion tore its prey to store it, or clawed its prey and ate it, the owner pays full damage.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the last answer was rejected, the גמרא gives a brand-new way to read the ברייתא so it no longer clashes with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to say 'tore and ate', which would be a single act that שמואל treats differently. רב נחמן בר יצחק splits it into 'tore (to store)' or 'clawed and ate'. Both of these are normal lion behavior, so neither one contradicts שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches separate cases. The list is read as 'either this or that', not one combined event.
Tore its prey to set it aside for later.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the ברייתא as one lion doing both actions. רב נחמן בר יצחק's whole point is that these are two different cases, each with the same ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It teaches separate cases:
phrases.notes: Literally 'it teaches to the sides'. The ברייתא lists 'either this case or that case'.

phrases.english: where it tore its prey in order to set it aside,
or where it clawed its prey and ate it –
it pays full damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to the challenge from step 8, after the answer in step 11 was rejected in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the structure of the ברייתא (a disjunctive list)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא describes one act of tearing and eating, which would contradict שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא lists two separate typical behaviors: tearing to store, or clawing and eating. Both pay full damage.

steps.title: רבינא: שמואל was talking about a tame lion
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that שמואל's ruling deals with a tame lion. It follows רבי אלעזר, who holds that attacking is not the normal way of a tame wild animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: When שמואל gave his ruling, he was talking about a tame lion, and he was following רבי אלעזר, who says attacking is not its normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a different approach. He says שמואל's case is about a tame lion, following the opinion of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a wild lion, killing and eating is normal, so the damage counts as eating (שן). For a tame lion, רבי אלעזר says attacking is not its way, so the attack counts as goring (קרן). That is why the owner would be liable even in רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not its normal way.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
When Shmuel says his ruling –
it is about a tame lion,
and according to Rabbi Elazar –
who says: it is not its normal way.
phrases.notes: He means that for a tame wild animal, attacking is not normal behavior.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent way to defend שמואל, instead of רב נחמן בר יצחק's rereading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (tame lion) and tying it to a specific opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's ruling is about an ordinary wild lion.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's case is a tame lion according to רבי אלעזר, so its attack counts as unusual behavior.

steps.title: Then clawing should also make the owner liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רבינא. If the lion is tame and attacking is not its way, then even clawing and eating should make the owner liable, but שמואל exempts that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even when it clawed and ate, the owner should also be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבינא's explanation. It shows that this explanation does not fit the other half of שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל exempted a lion that clawed and ate in רשות הרבים, because that is normal for a lion. But for a tame lion according to רבי אלעזר, no attack is normal. So clawing should also count as unusual, and the owner should be liable. רבינא's reading cannot explain why שמואל exempts it.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. If we accept what you just said.

phrases.english: If so,
then even when it clawed, the owner should also be liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אֲפִילּוּ דָּרְסָה נָמֵי לִיחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's explanation from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that שמואל was talking about a tame lion according to רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no attack is normal for a tame lion, then clawing should be unusual too. That would make the owner liable, but שמואל rules that clawing and eating is exempt.

steps.title: רבינא's statement was really about the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that רבינא's idea does not fit שמואל. It moves the statement to the ברייתא: the ברייתא is about a tame lion according to רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבינא's statement was not said about שמואל, but about the ברייתא. When the ברייתא teaches its ruling, it is talking about a tame lion, according to רבי אלעזר, who says attacking is not its normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by saying רבינא was explaining the ברייתא, not שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now שמואל's ruling stays about a normal wild lion, so clawing and eating stays exempt. The ברייתא that seemed to clash with him deals with a different case: a tame lion according to רבי אלעזר. Since the two sources talk about different lions, the ברייתא no longer contradicts שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said, meaning the statement was originally stated about this.
Here it means the ברייתא quoted earlier.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to defend שמואל from the ברייתא. (1) רב נחמן בר יצחק: the ברייתא lists two separate typical cases. (2) רבינא: the ברייתא is about a tame lion according to רבי אלעזר. רבינא's statement belongs to the ברייתא, not to שמואל. The next steps test this second way, and it ends with an unanswered קשיא in step 20.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not get mixed up and apply רבינא's 'tame lion' idea to שמואל. The גמרא just showed that it fails there. It only applies to the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rather, Ravina's statement
was not said about Shmuel,
but rather about the baraita;
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from step 8, about a lion in the victim's yard.

phrases.english: when the baraita teaches its ruling –
it is about a tame lion,
and according to Rabbi Elazar,
who says: it is not its normal way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּרָבִינָא לָאו אַשְּׁמוּאֵל אִתְּמַר אֶלָּא אַמַּתְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 15 by moving רבינא's statement from שמואל to the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving a statement to a different source
steps.terutzMaskana: רבינא was explaining the ברייתא. It deals with a tame lion according to רבי אלעזר, so it does not contradict שמואל.

steps.title: A tame lion's attack should pay only half
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא is about a tame lion, its attack is unusual, so it is like קרן and should pay only חצי נזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should only have to pay half damages!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from step 16, that the ברייתא is about a tame lion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, attacking is not normal behavior for a tame animal. Unusual damage belongs to קרן, and a first-time קרן pays only חצי נזק. But the ברייתא says the lion pays full damages.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if what you said is true)
Half the cost of the damage

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if the ברייתא is about a tame lion, for whom attacking is unusual.

phrases.english: he should have to pay half damages!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, חֲצִי נֶזֶק בָּעֵי לְשַׁלּוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reassignment of רבינא's idea to the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is about a tame lion according to רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unusual behavior counts as קרן, and a first-time קרן pays only half. Yet the ברייתא requires full payment.

steps.title: The lion was already a מועד
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a lion that was already forewarned, so it pays full damages.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the lion was forewarned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this tame lion had already attacked enough times to become a מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a קרן-type damage pays in full once the animal is a מועד. So the full payment in the ברייתא fits the tame-lion reading after all.

phrases.english: Where it was forewarned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (the lion was a מועד).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tame lion was a first-time attacker, so it should pay half.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tame lion had become a מועד, so it pays full damages.

steps.title: Then why is it listed under שן?
steps.stepSummary: If this is really a forewarned קרן case, the ברייתא should have listed it under the offshoots of קרן, not of שן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the ברייתא teach it among the offshoots of שן? It should have taught it among the offshoots of קרן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 18 from a different angle: where the case appears in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the lion was a מועד means the case is really קרן. But the ברייתא puts it in the list of תולדות of שן, which suggests it is normal eating behavior. That placement does not fit the tame-lion reading.

keyTerms.meaning: An offshoot (a subcategory of a main type of damage)
Tooth: damage done by eating, done for the animal's own benefit

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if this is a forewarned tame lion, which is really a קרן case.

phrases.english: why is it that it teaches it
among the offshoots of Tooth?
It should have taught it among the offshoots of Horn!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי הַאי דְּקָתָנֵי לַהּ גַּבֵּי תּוֹלָדָה דְשֵׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge against the answer of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The tame-lion-that-is-a-מועד reading of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A forewarned tame lion is a קרן case, but the ברייתא lists it under שן.

steps.title: The difficulty stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits it has no answer to the question about where the case is listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves step 19's question unanswered and ends this discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קשיא means the challenge stands and the tame-lion reading of the ברייתא has a real problem. It does not say the reading is fully rejected. It is just left with a question that was not resolved.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a difficulty (a question left unanswered)

steps.confusionAlert: קשיא here does not mean the explanation is fully thrown out, the way תיובתא would. It just means this question was never answered.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's lion pays full damages. Reading it as a tame, forewarned lion explains the full payment. But it cannot explain why the case is listed under שן, so that question stays open.

phrases.english: It is a difficulty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concedes that step 19's challenge has no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The tame-lion reading of the ברייתא remains with an unanswered difficulty.

steps.title: The משנה: the difference between a תם and a מועד
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה says a תם pays half damages, only from its own body, while a מועד pays full damages from the owner's best property.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: What is the difference between an innocuous ox and a forewarned ox? Only that the innocuous ox pays half damages from its own body, and the forewarned ox pays full damages from the best property.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks how a תם differs from a מועד and gives two differences.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two differences. The first is the amount: a תם pays half and a מועד pays full. The second is where the money comes from: for a תם the payment comes only from the damaging ox itself, while for a מועד the owner must pay from his best-quality property.

keyTerms.meaning: An innocuous animal, one not yet warned about
A forewarned animal, one that has a pattern of damaging
From its own body (only from the value of the ox itself)

steps.whyThisMatters: These two differences in amount and source of payment are the basic rules of תם and מועד, which the coming גמרא will analyze.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
What is the difference between an innocuous one and a forewarned one?
Only that the innocuous one pays
half damages from its body,
phrases.notes: The owner pays only up to the value of the ox that did the damage, not from his other property.

phrases.english: and the forewarned one pays full damages
from the best property.
phrases.notes: Literally 'from the upper.' He means the owner's best-quality land or goods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion ended with a קשיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תם pays half damages from its own body, and a מועד pays full damages from the owner's best property.

steps.title: What does 'עלייה' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking what the word 'עלייה' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is meant by 'עלייה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the new משנה by asking about one word: 'עלייה.' This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a מועד pays from the owner's 'עלייה' property. The word literally sounds like 'upper' or 'higher,' so the גמרא wants to know exactly what kind of property that is.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'upper/higher'; the משנה's word for the property a מועד pays from

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is 'aliyya'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה quoted in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word 'עלייה' in the משנה.

steps.title: It means the best-quality property
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that 'עלייה' means the best-quality items of the owner's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It means with the best of his property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers: 'עלייה' does not mean physically higher property, it means the best-quality property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Higher' is read as 'higher in quality.' So the owner of a מועד must pay the damages from his finest assets, not from whatever is worst.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
With the best of his property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עלייה' means the best-quality property of the owner.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines how a מועד's owner pays: from his finest assets.

steps.title: Support from the burial of חזקיהו
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says חזקיהו was buried 'במעלה' of the graves of דוד's descendants, and רבי אלעזר explains that means next to the best of the family, דוד and שלמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it says: 'And חזקיהו lay with his fathers, and they buried him in the מעלה of the graves of the sons of דוד.' And רבי אלעזר said: 'במעלה' means next to the best of the family. And who are they? דוד and שלמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to show that the word 'מעלה' (from the same root as 'עלייה') can mean 'the best.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק about חזקיהו, 'במעלה' is not a physical height but a place of honor, next to the greatest of the family. This shows the root עלה is used for 'best quality,' supporting רבי אלעזר's reading of 'עלייה.'

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says (introduces a supporting פסוק)
In the 'higher' place; here, next to the most honored

phrases.english: And so it says:
'And Hezekiah lay with his fathers,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 32:33

phrases.english: and they buried him in the best of the graves of David's descendants,'
And Rabbi Elazar said:
'Bema'ale' means next to the best of the family,
and who are they? David and Solomon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's definition in step 23 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק about חזקיהו's burial 'במעלה,' explained by רבי אלעזר as next to the most honored, דוד and שלמה.
steps.whatToRemember: 'עלייה' = the best property. The proof is that 'מעלה' in the burial of חזקיהו means the most honored place.

steps.title: What were the 'spices and זנים' at אסא's burial?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another burial פסוק, about a king laid on a bed full of 'בשמים וזנים,' and asks what that means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they buried him in his graves which he dug for himself in the city of דוד, and laid him on the bed that was filled with spices and זנים.' What is 'spices and זנים'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another burial פסוק of a king and asks what the unusual word 'זנים' means. This sets up a disagreement in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is no longer about paying damages. Since רבי אלעזר explained one burial פסוק, the גמרא continues with another burial פסוק that he and רבי שמואל בר נחמני explain.

keyTerms.meaning: An unusual word in the פסוק, explained in the next step

phrases.english: 'And they buried him in his graves
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 16:14, about King אסא.

phrases.english: which he had dug for himself in the city of David,
and they laid him on the bed
that was filled with spices and zenim' —
What is 'spices and zenim'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the burial פסוק of step 24 to another king's burial פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'זנים' in the פסוק.

steps.title: Many kinds of spices, or spices that lead to immorality
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says 'זנים' means many kinds of spices; רבי שמואל בר נחמני says they were spices that bring anyone who smells them to זימה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: All kinds of types. רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: Spices that anyone who smells them comes to זימה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different readings of the word 'זנים.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads 'זנים' as 'זיני,' meaning kinds, so the bed had many varieties of spices. רבי שמואל בר נחמני connects 'זנים' to the root of זימה (immorality), so these were spices whose smell stirs a person to immorality.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: Many kinds and kinds.
Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:
Spices that anyone who smells them
comes to licentiousness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר: many kinds of spices. רבי שמואל בר נחמני: spices that lead to זימה.

steps.title: What 'pit' was dug to trap ירמיהו?
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'they dug a pit to trap me,' רבי אלעזר says they suspected him of a זונה, and רבי שמואל בר נחמני says they suspected him of an אשת איש.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For they dug a pit to trap me, and hid snares for my feet.' רבי אלעזר said: They suspected him of a זונה. רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: They suspected him of a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more פסוק where the same two אמוראים disagree, this time about what trap was set for ירמיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the 'pit' was a false accusation of a sexual sin. They argue only about how serious it was: a זונה according to רבי אלעזר, or the more severe אשת איש according to רבי שמואל בר נחמני.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who had forbidden relations

steps.whatToRemember: After explaining 'עלייה' as the best property, the גמרא strings together verses where רבי אלעזר and רבי שמואל בר נחמני argue: the 'זנים' spices and the 'pit' dug for ירמיהו.

phrases.english: 'For they dug a pit to trap me,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 18:22

phrases.english: and hid snares for my feet' —
Rabbi Elazar said: They suspected him of a zona.
Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:
They suspected him of a married woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another verse disputed by the same two אמוראים from step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'pit' was a false suspicion: of a זונה (רבי אלעזר) or of an אשת איש (רבי שמואל בר נחמני).

steps.title: Why would an accusation about a married woman be called a pit
steps.stepSummary: The word 'pit' fits the view that they accused ירמיהו of a זונה, since a זונה is called a deep pit. But how does it fit the view that they accused him of an אשת איש?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says they accused him of a זונה, because a פסוק calls a זונה a deep pit. But for the one who says they accused him of an אשת איש, why use the word 'pit'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמואל בר נחמני's opinion from step 27. The word 'pit' in ירמיהו's complaint seems to fit only רבי אלעזר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירמיהו said 'they dug a pit to trap me.' משלי says 'a זונה is a deep pit,' so 'pit' points to a זונה. That supports רבי אלעזר and seems to leave רבי שמואל בר נחמני's אשת איש reading without support from the wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (for one side, but not for the other)
That they suspected him (falsely accused him)
A woman who had forbidden relations

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about ירמיהו actually sinning. Both opinions agree that it was a false accusation made by his enemies. The question is only which accusation the word 'pit' describes.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
that they suspected him of a זונה,
this is what is written:
"For a זונה is a deep pit."
phrases.notes: משלי 23:27

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
that they suspected him of a married woman,
what is the meaning of "pit"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two opinions of step 27 against the word 'pit' in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמואל בר נחמני's view that they accused ירמיהו of an אשת איש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Pit' is the פסוק's word for a זונה, so it seems to match only the זונה opinion.

steps.title: A married woman who sins is also called a זונה
steps.stepSummary: An אשת איש is not taken out of the category of זונה, so 'pit' fits her too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just because she is married, is she no longer included in the category of זונה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A married woman who sins can also be called a זונה, so the word 'pit' fits her as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that 'זונה' and 'אשת איש' are two separate groups. The answer says the word זונה is broad enough to include a married woman who sins. So the פסוק about a 'pit' works for רבי שמואל בר נחמני's opinion too.

keyTerms.meaning: Just because / is it so that? (introduces a rhetorical question)

phrases.english: Just because she is a married woman,
does she leave the category of זונה?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ מִי נָפְקָא מִכְּלַל זוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widening a term: the word זונה includes a sinning married woman.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Pit' refers only to a זונה, so it excludes the אשת איש reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: An אשת איש who sins is also called a זונה, so 'pit' fits both opinions.

steps.title: Why would an accusation about a זונה be called a plot to kill
steps.stepSummary: 'To kill me' fits the אשת איש view, since that sin carries the death penalty. But how does it fit the זונה view?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says they accused him of an אשת איש, because ירמיהו says they plotted to kill him. But for the one who says they accused him of a זונה, why does he say 'to kill me'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא challenges the other side, רבי אלעזר. ירמיהו says their plan was to have him killed, and that seems to fit only the אשת איש accusation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sinning with an אשת איש is punishable by death in בית דין, so a false accusation like that is really a plot to kill. Sinning with a זונה carries no death penalty in בית דין. So how could ירמיהו call that accusation a plot 'to kill me'?

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
that they suspected him of a married woman,
this is what is written:
"And You, ה׳, know
all their plotting against me, to kill me."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 18:23

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
that they suspected him of a זונה,
what is the meaning of "to kill me"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שֶׁחֲשָׁדוּהוּ מֵאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 28: now the other opinion is tested against a different word.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's view that they accused ירמיהו of a זונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A זונה accusation carries no death penalty, so it cannot be called a plot 'to kill.'

steps.title: To kill refers to throwing him into a muddy pit
steps.stepSummary: 'To kill me' does not refer to the accusation. It refers to their throwing ירמיהו into a pit of mud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to the fact that they threw him into a pit of mud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'to kill me' is about a different act of theirs: throwing ירמיהו into a muddy pit to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'to kill me' had to describe the accusation itself. The answer separates the two: the accusation was about a זונה, and the plot to kill was the muddy pit. So רבי אלעזר's opinion still works.
steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions survive: an אשת איש who sins is also called a זונה (so 'pit' fits), and 'to kill me' refers to the muddy pit (so the זונה opinion fits).

phrases.english: That they threw him into a pit of mud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the reference: 'to kill me' refers to a different event.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'To kill me' describes the accusation, which fits only an אשת איש.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'To kill me' describes the muddy pit, so the זונה opinion stands.

steps.title: ירמיהו asks that his enemies' charity go to unworthy people
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the next part of the same פסוק: ירמיהו asked that even his enemies' charity go to unworthy people, so they would get no reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא explained: What does 'let them be made to stumble before You; in the time of Your anger deal with them' mean? ירמיהו said to הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the world, even when they give charity, make them stumble by giving to unworthy people, so they will not get reward for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new explanation of the end of ירמיהו's prayer. 'Make them stumble' means that their good deeds should not earn them reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Charity normally earns a person reward. ירמיהו asked that his enemies' charity reach people who don't deserve it, so it would bring them no reward. That is the 'stumbling' the פסוק asks for.

phrases.english: Rava expounded:
What is meant by what is written:
"Let them be made to stumble before You;
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 18:23, the same פסוק as 'to kill me.'

phrases.english: in the time of Your anger, deal with them"?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר יִרְמְיָה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Yirmiyah said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
even at the time when they give charity,
make them stumble with people
who are not worthy,
so that they will not receive reward for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the end of the same ירמיהו פסוק quoted in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Make them stumble' means their charity should go to unworthy recipients so that it earns them no reward.

steps.title: A ישיבה was set up at חזקיהו's grave
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the פסוק about חזקיהו's burial, the גמרא learns that the 'honor in his death' was a ישיבה set up at his grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they gave him honor in his death': this teaches that they set up a ישיבה at his grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the פסוק about חזקיהו's burial from step 24 and explains its next words. The honor they gave him was setting up Torah learning at his grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 explained where חזקיהו was buried. Now the rest of that פסוק, 'they gave him honor in his death,' is explained as a ישיבה placed at his grave. So the honor was Torah learning.

phrases.english: "And they gave him honor in his death":
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 32:33, the same פסוק about חזקיהו's burial from earlier.

phrases.english: this teaches that they set up a yeshiva at his grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ירמיהו discussion and returns to the חזקיהו burial פסוק from step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The honor given to חזקיהו at his death was a ישיבה set up at his grave.

steps.title: How long did the ישיבה at חזקיהו's grave last?
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן and the רבנן disagree about how long they learned at חזקיהו's grave. One opinion says three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן and the רבנן argue about this ישיבה. One of them says they learned there for three days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a detail to the ישיבה at חזקיהו's grave: there is a מחלוקת about how long it lasted. Only the first opinion, three days, appears here. The second opinion comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 33 told us that the honor was a ישיבה at the grave. Now the question is how long that honor lasted. The גמרא uses 'חד אמר' (one said), so we are not told which of the two holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree about it (here, about the ישיבה)
A תנא who argues with the רבנן here
One said, without telling us which one

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to match 'three' to רבי נתן or to the רבנן. The גמרא deliberately says 'one said' and does not tell us who.

phrases.english: They disagree about it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ישיבה at חזקיהו's grave from the step before.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan and the Rabbis:
one said: three,
phrases.notes: The גמרא just says 'three.' It means three days of learning at the grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail, how long it lasted, to the ישיבה at חזקיהו's grave described in step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת between רבי נתן and the רבנן about how long the ישיבה lasted. One says three days.
